newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Five Zulus killed in suspected political attack.
newsitem.headline: Five Zulus killed in suspected political attack.

text.p: Gunmen have shot or clubbed to death five people, including a 90-year-old woman, in a suspected political attack in South Africa's volatile Zulu province, police said on Sunday.

Spokesman Captain Bongani Nzimande said the attackers, armed with spears and AK-47 automatic rifles, attacked a home in the rural village of Lamont near Port Shepstone on the KwaZulu-Natal south coast on Saturday evening.
"There are five people who have been killed in their sleep," Nzimande told reporters, adding: "At this stage the motive for the massacre points to politics."
He said eight children who had been asleep in the home survived unhurt. "It appears this was a planned attack, focused only on the adults."
Nzimande said Lamont, a stronghold of Zulu Chief Mangosuthu Buthelezi's Inkatha Freedom Party (IFP), was tense on Sunday and additional police patrolled the area.

Inkatha are the main black rivals of President Nelson Mandela's African National Congress. Feuding between the two groups has fuelled violence in which about 15,000 people have been killed in KwaZulu-Natal in the last decade.

Violence monitors last week identified areas of the KwaZulu- Natal south coast as one of several potential flashpoints during the Christmas holidays, when men return to their homes in the province from jobs in the mining and industrial zone around Johannesburg.
Last Christmas day 18 people were killed in an attack on the ANC settlement of Shobashobane near Port Shepstone.
